audit.intended_rules: Ch.10 event-materials rule (note must name event AND state budget-owner pre-approval; missing either → deduct event lines) plus Ch.2 note-requirements for commercial invoices; distractor lines exercise the sub-€100 peripheral rule and the €50 incidental-supplies cap (both within limits).
consistency_issues: Item description 'Raspberry Pi 5 Model B (8GB RAM)' is not a real product name (the Pi 5 has no Model B variant); cosmetic, does not affect adjudication.
handbook_issues: 'Cables' appear in both the incidental-supplies consumables list (€50/invoice cap) and the sub-€100 peripherals list; here the supplies lines stay under the cap either way, but the overlap could produce divergent adjudications on other cases.
realism_issues: Minor: 'Pi 5 Model B' naming oddity; otherwise vendor (Darmstadt electronics distributor, DE tax ID, 19% VAT) and prices are realistic.
audit.notes: Validator passes (1/1 valid). No label.json or receipt.jpg. Correct adjudication: partial approval. Deduct the promotional line (branded glow-in-the-dark bottle openers, €96) with its VAT share (€18.24 at 19%) because the note names the Q2 developer meetup but does not state budget-owner pre-approval — both statements are required per Ch.10. Reimbursed = 680.68 - 114.24 = 566.44. Hardware lines (unit prices €89 and €17) are sub-€100 peripherals; supplies lines (€24 tape, €28 cable) fit within the €50 incidental-supplies cap. Buyer company differs from the firm name, but the Ch.10 FAQ explicitly waives buyer identity on commercial invoices. Fits subtle_single: deduction requires knowing one specific passage. No changes needed; consider fixing the 'Model B' product name if the case is ever regenerated.
